svg.text: sizes XS / S / M / L · one d20 per rule

g.text: 1. Pick a size preset: XS, S, M or L. Its column gives the d20 ranges.
2. Start with Start(): START and GOAL are its anchors.
3. While red nodes remain: pick one, roll d20, replace it with the diagram of its range.
Blue = node before it, teal = node after it. Edges keep their direction.
4. R() last, on its tier: early, middle or late by progress to the boss; late near a boss.
5. GB() on the theme's rewards. Objects (keys, switches, levers, item) are new per rule.
6. Finally merge neighbouring n / e / t / p / c rooms of one type on plain two-way paths.
Why it stays small and solvable:
• Only L() and S() recurse. Every other rule expands once into a fixed shape.
• Each lock rule places its key on a branch that forks before the lock.
• Odds keep the expected size finite (ρ below 1). As a cap, past
300 nodes or 200 expansions L() and S() take room and end.
room (terminal): n e t p c em eb gb
pickup: small key, boss key, dungeon item
state gate: open when all switches hit
toggle gate: open with the lever ON
toggle gate: open with the lever OFF
n nothing · e enemy · t trap · p puzzle · c challenge · em mini-boss · eb boss · gb bonus goal
Room chooser (terminal content) · rolled by progress to the boss, not by size
ρ: spectral radius of the expected-offspring matrix. Below 1 = finite expected size.
Bonus goal · dead end · the theme's rewards (zelda shown)
Toggle lever: ON opens the way, OFF opens a bonus
Dungeon item gate: mini-boss guards the item that opens the way
Boss key: opens the boss room

g.data-variant: BK boss key behind small key
